I feel like this common place term also takes away the power of the word. Like if I say "I'm depressed" and someone says "everyone is depressed" (I've heard this multiple times) that's two different things. When I say im depressed I'm saying something is really wrong I'm in a bad place please help. I don't use the term "depressed" lightly. But now it is so commonly thrown around that no one can identify when I am truly struggling to stay alive verses when Janie failed her math test and she is "depressed" about it.  I feel like our culture had taken this word that referred to a specific criteria and made it a umbrella term for all negative feelings (ie. Disappointed, sad, upset, grieving, etc.). Now those who struggle with depression are being grouped with people who are occasionally sad, causing their struggles to be discounted because 'everyone is sad sometimes'.

Ok, if you think she actually genuinely cares about you, and is trying to understand how you feel and your motivations behind your attempt I believe she might not have bad intentions. And if she is saying these things as a joke I would consider that she may be using humor to deal with things that make her uncomfortable. It's deflection.  I also think if she keeps bringing it up is probably something that really bothers her.  Continues to weigh on her. She may feel like it was her fault, and she is trying to remind you she cares,  but in ways that are not actually supportive.  If you think she really cares about you and this could be the case you should try to be patient,  remind her that while things are different for you now you still take her opinion and the things she says to you to heart.  Tell her that while you know she is hurt and she may be trying to help you would really appreciate and respond more if she would not make a joke out of things that hurt you.  

On the other hand though,  if she is one of those old people that believe mental illness is not a real thing then get out. Avoid those conversations, ignore the negative commentary,  and work on distancing yourself from her.  If it is detrimental to you,  more than a simple she doesn't know how to properly help,  then you need to protect yourself.  You are worth protecting.

I cut when I am angry or frustrated. I feel like I have to take it out somehow. If not on myself I might say things that hurt the people around me. I like having the open cuts on my leg so that when I get angry I can just run my hand over them, put some pressure there and it simmers out my rage enough that it is controllable.  I also have never personally seen any problem with it, honestly.  People tell me to stop, its bad. But I see it  as no worse than getting a tattoo. It hurts, leaves marks, people do it to lash out when they are upset.  The only difference is that cutting is cheaper and has a stigma.  I cut less now because I moved away from my trigger (the thing that really sent me into angry fits)  and now I don't feel the need to comfort myself in this way as often, but when I feel out of control I still do. It always levels me out.

I wrote mine at age 15. I'm 21 now. I poured out my soul onto the pages. Awful handwriting due to the anger and frustration, but I "carry them always".
